kind: Actual queued callback resolved-target code frequency from original-source battle
scope: One fixed callback-only original-source battle. After the unchanged snapshot(callback), a proved public-V8 metadata observer resolves the bound target without callback invocation, bind interception or replacement. Captured intrinsic Function.prototype.toString reads the actual function and resolved target source. Proxy/limit outcomes remain opaque. Original callback identity, queue loop and active helpers remain unchanged. Diagnostic code frequency, not performance or whole-program trace.

oracleProfile.wholeBattleContextReason: Reflect the real VM global object with ordinary Script var/function binding descriptors; contextified sandbox wrappers change configurability and hide uninitialized bindings from parent reflection.
oracleProfile.reason: Default JIT tiers and --no-opt produced different NaN bits for identical source and inputs. --jitless was stable across all six cold/warmed probe processes.
oracleProfile.throughputPolicy: Performance measurements may use compiled native candidates or separately identified runtime flags. Qualification compares candidate traces against this pinned source profile; measurements alone do not establish equivalence.
oracleProfile.scope: Reproducible reference implementation profile, not a claim that ECMAScript specifies NaN sign/payload or that all engine versions produce identical bits.

limitations: Target code equality does not imply identical bound receivers, arguments, captured bindings or behavior. The public API exposes target identity only; none of those values is inspected or copied.
Exact literal matches can be ambiguous; all matching original ranges are retained without claiming a unique closure creation site.
Frequency is executions, not CPU cost. Callback bodies may merely dispatch methods whose work is unmeasured here.
Original FIFO queue capture, shift, appended callbacks, before/after snapshots and callback invocation remain in the unchanged source drain.
Actor/effect/view lifecycle remains outside the callback-only adapter; one roster is not a random-battle qualification corpus.
